job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: Today in our geography lab, we explored the invisible blanket surrounding our planet. We started by analyzing a pie chart showing that nitrogen makes up 78% of the air, while oxygen is only 21%. Many students were surprised to learn that nitrogen is the most abundant gas, not oxygen, even though oxygen is vital for our survival. Next, we used a barometer to measure air pressure and discussed how the atmosphere extends hundreds of kilometers above the Earth's surface, far beyond the altitude where clouds form. We learned that the atmosphere is divided into distinct layers, and clouds are only found in the very lowest layer, the troposphere. Finally, we investigated water vapor. We learned that humidity is the invisible moisture present in the air even on sunny days. Humidity is not the same as rain; rain only occurs when that moisture condenses and falls. By the end of the lesson, we understood that the atmosphere is a complex system that supports life far beyond our immediate view of the sky.
response.summary: The atmosphere is composed mostly of nitrogen and extends far beyond the clouds. Humidity refers to invisible water vapor in the air, which is distinct from the event of rainfall.
